author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Brown University and Brown University Health are launching an aging-research partnership backed by a $37 million investment from the Starr Foundation.

The Starr Healthspan Innovation Alliance is designed to move discoveries from university laboratories into clinical trials across the health system. Brown said the work will focus on age-associated diseases and on extending the years people remain healthy, rather than treating longevity as a single condition.

Funding will expand Brown’s Center on the Biology of Aging, support laboratory research and help recruit scientists in geroscience, the study of genetic, molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in aging. The health system’s clinical network is expected to provide a pathway for evaluating potential treatments with patients.

The alliance matters regionally because it connects a major Rhode Island research university with the state’s largest health system. Its announced aims include work relevant to cancer and dementia, but the partnership did not announce a specific new therapy or guarantee clinical outcomes. Individual studies will still require their own scientific review, trial design and patient-safety oversight.
dek: Brown University and Brown University Health will link laboratory work with clinical trials through a new Starr Foundation-backed partnership.
headline: Brown launches $37 million alliance for aging research
